message.content:
**Image1** (grey, small panel): 3D density map render, viewed roughly TOP/side-on at an oblique angle — compact globular blob with lumpy surface; some small isolated fragments/blobs detached at the right edge (noise or dissociated micelle density). No clear detergent belt or ring; helix detail not resolved, just lumpy low-res features.

**Image2** (pale yellow): 3D density map render at an oblique/tilted view. Large connected density with holes and lobes, suggesting partial detergent belt/protein mix. Several small satellite blobs visible around the periphery (lower left, right). Some tube-like features hint at helices but not clearly resolved.

**Image3** (cyan): 3D map, oblique side-ish view. Large connected mass with protruding lumps; one small detached blob upper right. Density looks fragmented/patchy — moderate noise. Faint elongated features could be helices, but not crisp.

**Image4** (grey): 3D map, more TOP-like view down the particle. Roundish outline with many holes and lumpy density filling a disk — consistent with looking down onto a detergent/micelle disk with protein on top. Scattered small speckles around edges minor. No continuous helices visible; mostly lumpy topology.

**Image5** (pale yellow, larger panel): 3D map, clear TOP view down the micelle/detergent disk: a roughly circular, ring-like arrangement of lumpy density with holes, protein domains seen end-on. Few isolated blobs; fairly clean. Internal detail is lumpy but individual helices not well defined — reads as top-down micelle view.

**Image6** (cyan): two separate densities in one frame — a small smooth blob on the left (likely a detached micelle or fragment) and a larger lumpy map on the right, viewed obliquely. The right map has hole-ridden lumpy topology, some possible helix-like rods. Speckle noise minimal but the split into two objects is notable.

**Image7** (light purple/lavender): 3D map, TOP view — circular disk of very lumpy, noodle-like density filling the whole disk, typical of looking down a detergent belt with protein. Dense speckled lumps; no isolated external blobs. Helix detail questionable — many short rod-like lumps that could be helices seen end-on, but noisy.

**Image8** (grey): 3D map, TOP view — a filled circular disk of very fine grainy/speckled density (much higher noise level, lower threshold or noisier map). No clean ring or belt; speckle noise dominates. No resolvable helices.

**Image9** (pale yellow): 3D map, TOP view — circular disk of fine speckled/lumpy density, similar to image8 but yellow. Slightly clumpier center. Speckle noise prominent; no isolated external blobs; helix detail not resolved.

**Image10** (cyan): 3D map, TOP/oblique view — elliptical disk of fine granular density with abundant scattered speckle dots around and above it (clear noise/spray of small blobs). Least clean image; no helix detail, just a fuzzy grainy blob.

**Image11** (grey, larger panel): 3D map, TOP view — circular disk filled with coarse lumpy density, holes around the rim suggesting a detergent ring edge. Cleaner than 8–10, but still quite granular; short rod-like lumps hint at helices/end-on helix bundles but not clearly resolved; few isolated blobs outside the main disk.

**Summary pattern:** images 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 are TOP views down the micelle disk (ring/disk appearance); images 1, 2, 3, 6 are oblique/side-ish views of the particle; image 4 is intermediate/top-like. Noise/speckle is worst in 8, 9, 10; cleanest are 1, 5, 6. None show a crisp side-view detergent belt with vertically crossed helices — most side-ish views are too lumpy for resolved helices.
